prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computer science and programming (recommended)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to problem-solving in the field of engineering, including the calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Understand the operation of hydraulic machines, both lifting and receiving, based on the fundamentals of fluid mechanics.
Design hydraulic machine installations, manage their operation, and technically direct complete fluid pumping systems and energy generation with hydraulic turbines.

syllabus_topics: Block I. HYDRAULIC TURBOMACHINERY. ROTARY AND POSITIVE DISPLACEMENT MACHINES
Topic 1. Classification of hydraulic machines: Turbomachinery. Rotary and positive displacement pumps
Topic 6. Water hammer in pumping systems
Topic 8. Reaction turbines: Francis, Propeller and Kaplan
Topic 9. Energy generation: hydroelectric and wind power plants
Practice I. Complex pumping systems: series-parallel pumps
Practice III. Testing of a Pelton turbine
Practice IV. Testing of a Kaplan turbine
Problems on the fundamental equation of turbomachinery
assessment_rules: For ordinary examination, continuous assessment accounts for 40% and a final exam for 60% of the final grade. Alternatively, students can opt for a single final assessment weighing 100%, consisting of a problems section (60%) and a theory section (40%), forfeiting continuous assessment grades. For extraordinary examination, continuous assessment grades from the ordinary call are carried over, allowing students to retake only the problems part of the exam, or they can opt for the single final assessment under the same conditions as the ordinary call. To pass the course, a final grade of at least 5 out of 10 is required, along with a minimum of 3 out of 10 in the problems part of the exam.
